class.name: RealityVolumeCamera3D
class.brief_description: Defines a cube that fits into a volumetric window on visionOS.
class.description:
On visionOS, the camera is controlled by the OS rather than the game. However you can still translate/rotate/scale the scene to emulate a video game camera.
The RealityVolumeCamera3D represents a cube volume that you can place anywhere in your scene; you can also change its transform every frame if you want a dynamic camera.
The GodotRealityKit extension will apply the inverse transform of the camera to your scene, so that this cube fits into its volumetric window on visionOS.
The RealityVolumeCamera3D is only used in windowed mode on visionOS; in immersive mode, use an XROrigin instead.

method.name: get_camera_projection
method.description: Returns the camera projection type. Always returns [constant Camera3D.PROJECTION_ORTHOGONAL].

method.name: get_camera_transform
method.description: Returns the global transform of the internal camera used for rendering.

method.name: get_frustum
method.description: Returns the camera frustum planes in world space.

method.name: get_window_measured_size
method.description: Returns the physical size, in meters, that visionOS reports for the volume this camera's [Window] opens as. Returns [code]Vector3(0, 0, 0)[/code] until the volume is shown, and again after it closes; use [member window_size] until then.

method.name: is_position_behind
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param world_point] is behind the camera.

method.name: is_position_in_frustum
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param world_point] is inside the camera frustum.

method.name: make_current
method.description: Makes this volume camera the active camera for the current viewport.

method.name: project_local_ray_normal
method.description: Returns the local-space ray direction for an orthographic projection. Always returns [code]Vector3(0, 0, -1)[/code].

method.name: project_position
method.description: Returns the world-space position for a given [param screen_point] at distance [param z_depth] from the camera.

method.name: project_ray_normal
method.description: Returns the world-space ray direction for [param screen_point]. For orthographic projection this is the camera's forward direction.

method.name: project_ray_origin
method.description: Returns the world-space ray origin for [param screen_point].

method.name: unproject_position
method.description: Returns the screen-space position for a given [param world_point].

members.member: Which axis to preserve when the viewport aspect ratio doesn't match the volume.
If [code]true[/code], a preview [Camera3D] is generated so the editor viewport can preview the volume camera's view.
The largest physical size, in meters, the person can resize the volume to when its [Window] opens as a volume. Zero components leave that dimension unbounded.
The smallest physical size, in meters, the person can resize the volume to when its [Window] opens as a volume. Zero components leave that dimension unbounded.

The physical size of the volume, in meters, when its [Window] opens as a volume. In the [b]2D Window[/b] presentation style, a [Window] holding this camera opens as a RealityKit volume; set [member Window.unresizable] to keep this size.
Size of the volume relative to the Node itself. There is a gizmo displaying the cube in the editor, so that you can preview what is inside and outside the volume.

signal.name: window_resized
signal.description: Emitted when the physical size of the volume changes, with the new size in meters: when it opens, when the person resizes it, and with [code]Vector3(0, 0, 0)[/code] when it closes (see [method get_window_measured_size]).
